newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia stocks end with most gains intact.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia stocks end with most gains intact.

text.p: SPI Futures 2448 +13 US 30yr cl 6.83 -0.04
10yrbond futs 92.200 +0.030 Gold NY 352.75 Lon fix 354.50
*Stocks end stronger, slip from early highs after initial buying enthusiasm wanes, banks lead. Volume 325.13 million, value A$676.51 million, 1,082 stocks traded, 312 steady, 441 up, 329 down.
The Australian share market closed stronger on Thursday but slipped from its early Wall Street-inspired highs as initial buying enthusiasm eased.
By 4.25 p.m. (0525 GMT), the All Ordinaries index was 14.4 points higher at 2,447.4.
The March share index futures contract was up 13 points at 2,448, a 0.6 point premium to the underlying index.

The market exploded out of the blocks, ignited by U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan's calming comments to U.S. markets, before upside interest moderated and solid gains were consolidated in a day of modest trade.
"It was a good performance even if we couldn't keep the starting pace up," said a Melbourne-based dealer.
The big banks led the way with Comonwealth Bank, up 22.3 cents to A$12.95, and National Australia Bank, up 13 cents to A$16.36, the pick of the big four bunch.
"Commonwealth Bank and NAB were the main contributors today," the dealer said.
Also lending assistance was a strong showing from CRA, up 18 cents to A$19.00, after its dual listed sibling RTZ, climbed higher in London trade on Wednesday.
Infrastructure investor, Australian Infrastructure Group made its debut at A$2.32, a 32 cent premium to its issue price and closed at A$2.27.

Novus Petroleum shares bounced back from their recent selldown, jumping 35 cents to A$3.30, with traders saying exploration potential rather than Wednesday's sharply higher year profit result fuelled the rise.

Foster's Brewing Group topped turnover with over 10.6 million shares traded, the bulk of it on one line of 9.25 million shares, in what brokers said was normal institutional business. Foster's shares closed steady at A$2.67.
Results continued apace with gas distributor AGL adding nine cents to A$7.45 after reporting a 19.6 percent higher half year net profit of A$75.6 million.

Paper and packaging giant Amcor lost 14 cents to A$8.35 after posting a sharply lower first half net profit of A$140.6 million, while radio network operator Austereo added three cents to A$2.28 in thin trade after its 11 percent higher first half net profit of A$17.15 million.
Vintner BRL Hardy closed a cent higher at A$3.16 after its 33 percent higher year net profit of A$23.06 million.
Cinema and theme park operator, Village Roadshow, posted a 27 percent higher first half net profit of A$26.1 million. Its shares added a cent to close at A$4.26.
Rises outnumbered falls by a ratio of about seven to five, while about 29 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
FUTURES/OPTIONS - Futures trade was active, although slower than the hectic trade seen on Wednesday. Options trade was light.
